episodes.154693: A warm front across central Florida on 2/6 lifted northward as a surface low developed along the front in the eastern Gulf of Mexico. The warm front progressed northward to just south of the I-10 corridor during the night 2/6 into the early morning hours of 2/7 as the surface low track east along the front and then offshore of the local Atlantic coast early in the morning 2/7. Very strong shear was in place across the area with elevated instability with mid level lapse rates 7-7.5 deg C/km.  Some wind damage with gusts of 40-50 mph was reported as well as hail as large as quarter size. Widespread rainfall of 2-4 inches occurred in a couple of swaths across NE FL within 24 hrs which produced some localized flooding.
episodes.154727: A thunderstorm produced a brief, weak tornado (landspout) in Vero Lakes Estates, resulting in minor damage to fences and trees.
episodes.155173: An upper level trough dived south which helped to move a stalled out boundary over north Florida through the state. As it did the front produced strong thunderstorms and marine wind gust.
episodes.155259: A front moving from the west and northwest brought heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms to the islands, and some hail to the Big Island.  The rain caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.155261: A waterspout was spotted about one mile northeast of Hawaiian Beaches on the Big Island of Hawaii.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.

events.narrative: Nickel-sized hail reported from a thunderstorm developing over the eastern part of the island of Hawaii.

Minor damage occurred to a home in Keystone Heights with minor to some moderate tree damage. The time of damage was based on radar. The cost of damage was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.
Two homes received minor to moderate roof damage. Multiple trees and powerlines down between Chiefland and Fanning Springs.

Based on radar, video, and eyewitness reports received from the public, a brief EF-0 tornado (landspout) occurred in Vero Lakes Estates. Peak estimated wind speeds were between 65 and 70 mph. The landspout tornado formed at approximately 1612 LST at 100th Avenue, just north of 77th Street, in Vero Lakes Estates. The tornado traveled a relatively short distance, moving almost due north along 100th Avenue, then dissipated just before reaching 79th Street at approximately 1613 LST. Several properties sustained minor fence damage and many had unsecured backyard items scattered around. There was also minor tree damage along the street.
